key_insight: Welded stainless-clad 304/Q235B rectangular tubes sealed with 304 stainless end plates can approach all-stainless corrosion performance, but weld design strongly controls both mechanical behavior and corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: The results support using stainless-clad bimetallic steel for cost-effective corrosion-resistant structural components in marine and other aggressive environments.
method: Compared three welding process schemes for tube-to-end-plate joints.
Evaluated hardness/mechanical performance and indoor salt-spray accelerated corrosion behavior.
Fitted corrosion mass-loss data and built a marine-atmosphere corrosion prediction model.
evidence_signal: All joints had maximum hardness below 280 HV, the best corrosion resistance came from TIG + ER308, and the corrosion fit showed strong agreement (R² > 0.98) with a power-law trend.
watch_item: Weld intersections were the most corrosion-prone regions, so joint geometry, filler selection, and weld quality control remain critical for field deployment.
paper_title: Evaluation of the Corrosion Resistance of Welded Joints of Stainless-Clad 304/Q235B Bimetallic Steel Rectangle Tubes and 304 Stainless-Steel End Plates
